description: Implement reusable mohist/agent Workflow execution with durable AgentJob and AgentSession lineage, shared admission, stable lifecycle results, and Workflow-owned arbitration.

tasks.title: Materialize the Workflow Agent handoff and immutable launch lineage
tasks.description: Replace the current mohist/agent-to-runtime translation with the durable agent-handoff envelope while keeping profile validation virtual, task-only, and independent of live Agent existence. Treat agent-handoff as temporary non-execution transport with an explicit POST request/accepted-rejected-retry acknowledgement contract, a command/fingerprint fence persisted before live preflight, and a report path that never enters ordinary Workflow task/check reporting. Persist the original preflight rejection and Workflow failure application under that fence so replay cannot accept after Agent state changes. Add the Server handoff service and coordinator extension that resolve the active Agent, readiness, workspace, and immutable execution snapshot, then prepare, promote, verify, and idempotently accept one AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, and AgentTurn lineage for each TaskRun attempt. Keep participants nonclaimable until Workflow acceptance, accept Session lineage before issuing one final idempotent AgentJob activation/admission command, and route every post-acceptance activation failure through the same terminal AgentJob delivery instead of directly failing Workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: Profile validation accepts mohist/agent only for tasks, requires literal name and prompt strings, allows only name/prompt/session/timeout, and does not query live Agent state; checks and invalid inputs are rejected with actionable errors.

A claimed mohist/agent task produces an agent-handoff transport dispatch rather than mohist/opencode or mohist/pi; the Runner submits the typed handoff command with commandId=workId and a request fingerprint, and accepted/rejected/retry acknowledgements retire or retain only that transport work.

Agent resolution follows the canonical agent_* id-only and name-first fallback rules; missing, archived, or readiness-rejected Agents may reject after a transient transport claim but create no accepted AgentJob/AgentSession/SessionInput/AgentTurn lineage, Agent concurrency admission, or external Runtime work; the coordinator durably stores the original rejection before applying the normal Workflow failure/recovery boundary through ApplyAgentHandoffRejectionAsync, and replay returns that rejection even if Agent state later changes.

An accepted attempt persists one immutable Agent snapshot, one WorkflowAgentInvocation, and mutually locatable Job, Session, Input, and Turn identifiers; replay returns those identities without submitting a duplicate prompt.

The coordinator prepares and verifies the complete participant set as hidden nonclaimable work before Workflow acceptance, then acknowledges non-executing Session acceptance before one final AgentJob activation/admission command. A failure before Workflow acceptance aborts the provisional set; a definitive failure after acceptance terminalizes the same AgentJob and reaches Workflow only through PendingWorkflowTerminalDelivery, while an uncertain response after activation or claim resumes the same command and can never fail a live Job by inference; direct Agent launches, Inline Agent Actions, and checks retain their existing behavior.

Focused Server and Runner tests cover virtual validation, typed handoff request/acknowledgement routing, fingerprint replay/conflict, preflight rejection replay after Agent recovery, rejection failure/recovery application, Agent selection, readiness rejection, snapshot isolation, provisional preparation/verification and abort, failure after Session acceptance, definitive rejection before AgentJob admission, lost activation response after permit/ledger creation and Runner claim, terminal activation-failure delivery, permit release, lineage creation, and idempotent redelivery.
tasks.output: Server and Runner support for the durable agent-handoff path, immutable WorkflowAgentInvocation lineage, and passing contract/admission tests.
tasks.notes: Keep AgentRefResolver, AgentReadinessService, named Workspace resolution, AgentLaunchCoordinatorGrain, and AgentJobGrain as the authoritative seams; the coordinator must persist the command fence before preflight, retain rejection_pending with the original error, replay the resolved snapshot rather than re-read mutable Agent or Project state, keep participants nonclaimable until Workflow acceptance, and never directly fail Workflow after AgentJob becomes the accepted execution owner.

tasks.title: Execute Agent-backed Workflow tasks with completion side effects
tasks.description: Add the Runner agent-handoff execution branch and extend the canonical AgentJob dispatch with the frozen Agent execution definition, turn deadline, workspace identity, and complete WorkflowTaskContract/finalizerKey. Run OpenCode or Pi only through the existing AgentJob executor, then prepare and transmit one typed WorkflowAgentFinalizationRequest in the existing agent-job /report contract: the Runner completion adapter evaluates expect and _output against the structured Agent result and workspace and uploads artifacts through the invocation-keyed route, while the Server-side WorkflowAgentFinalizer owns invocation-keyed artifact binding, setVars mutation, and Workflow task application without making AgentSession transcript events authoritative. Add a typed accepted/stale/retry/rejected/conflict AgentJob acknowledgement that the Runner must inspect, and terminalize an active Job with a frozen-contract invalid-report failure before returning settled rejection.
acceptanceCriteria: The Runner does not resolve mohist/agent through ActionRegistry or start a runtime for the handoff; it renders and validates the envelope, sends POST /api/runner/{runnerId}/agent-handoffs with the stable commandId/fingerprint, never sends the handoff to /report, and retires the handoff only after an accepted or definitive rejection acknowledgement whose Workflow failure/recovery application has completed, while retaining it for retry otherwise.

AgentJob dispatch carries the snapshotted runtime, model, variant, ordered Skills, instructions, Job/Session/Input/Turn references, Workflow owner identity, workspace binding, and the validated per-turn timeout; Workflow input cannot override Agent execution properties.

Named workspace materialization and home-Runner affinity use the persisted workspace identity, including delayed materialization and unavailable-home behavior, without substituting a raw Runner directory.

The Runner completion adapter evaluates expect against the structured Agent result and persisted workspace, treats _output as final assistant text, extracts capturedOutputs and setVars, and uploads artifacts with (workflowRunId, taskRunId, jobId, finalizerKey) identity; it sends the typed finalization envelope through the existing agent-job /report field, while the Server validates and durably stores it before applying the requested terminal result. A valid first report returns accepted, a same-payload replay returns stale, transient or malformed acknowledgements retain awaitingAck, a conflicting terminal payload returns settled conflict, and an invalid active report first terminalizes the Job with a frozen-contract failure before returning settled rejected. The Server-side WorkflowAgentFinalizer calls BindAgentInvocationAsync to create visible WorkflowArtifact rows, write the invocation-keyed WorkflowAgentArtifactBindReceipt, and remove pending uploads exactly once, applies setVars through a keyed mutation command, records the bind receipt key and bound artifact ids in one finalizer receipt, and preserves recovery/retry semantics on postcondition or delivery failure.
OpenCode and Pi execution paths receive both Agent instructions and the Workflow prompt, while direct AgentJob execution and unrelated Workflow Actions remain unchanged.

Focused Runner, AgentJob, workspace, artifact, variable, and completion-evaluator tests cover OpenCode/Pi selection, timeout/default handling, delayed workspace materialization, _output, typed finalization report transport and validation, accepted/stale/retry/rejected/conflict settlement, HTTP-200 retry acknowledgements, malformed and unknown acknowledgements, invalid-report terminal failure, direct-Agent valid-report compatibility, duplicate/conflicting report replay, invocation-keyed artifact routing and binding, pending-upload cleanup, bind-receipt crash recovery, finalizer receipt replay/conflict, keyed setVars mutation, idempotent side effects, and postcondition failures.
tasks.output: AgentJob-backed Workflow execution with the frozen task contract, workspace/timeout handling, and passing Runner finalizer tests.
tasks.notes: Keep the Workflow task contract separate from the Agent execution snapshot. The Runner completion adapter prepares workspace-dependent facts and sends one optional workflowFinalization field through the existing AgentJob report boundary but never advances WorkflowRun; RunnerHost must inspect the typed AgentJob acknowledgement instead of treating any HTTP 200 as settlement. The Server-side WorkflowAgentFinalizer is the only durable side-effect bridge, and terminal delivery remains the next task.

tasks.title: Deliver terminal Agent results and arbitrate Workflow advancement
tasks.description: Extend AgentJob terminal state with one canonical PendingWorkflowTerminalDelivery carrying the immutable WorkflowAgentFinalizationRequest received through the validated agent-job report field, and make IWorkflowGrain.ApplyAgentJobFinalizationAsync the only guarded Server-side WorkflowAgentFinalizer operation for lineage-checked result and side-effect application. Define the typed accepted/stale/retry/rejected/conflict report settlement contract, invalid-report terminal failure, durable bind-receipt recovery before finalizer receipt completion, project AgentJob facts into queued, executing, recovering, completed, failed, and cancelled invocation states, preserve immutable terminal results and finalization receipts, release shared admission exactly once, and route success/failure/cancellation through existing Workflow completion and recovery boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentJob status maps to queued, executing, recovering, completed, failed, or cancelled using the documented rules, and nonterminal reads never fabricate a final result.

Workflow-owned terminal delivery persists one stable PendingWorkflowTerminalDelivery containing the complete WorkflowAgentFinalizationRequest and retries the single ApplyAgentJobFinalizationAsync operation on Retry; every delivery verifies WorkflowRun, TaskRun, Job, Session, Input, Turn, and finalizerKey identity, invokes BindAgentInvocationAsync for the supplied artifact ids, recovers an existing WorkflowAgentArtifactBindReceipt before writing the finalizer receipt, and stops on Accepted, Stale, or definitive Conflict with bound artifact ids retained in the receipt.

Duplicate terminal reports and late Runner reports are acknowledged as settled stale, conflicting terminal payloads are settled conflict, invalid active reports become a stable terminal failure before settled rejection, and none can rewrite an existing terminal Job, invocation result, or Workflow task; shared Agent concurrency resources are released once.
Unknown or uncertain post-claim work is non-claimable and recovering, reconciliation uses the original work identity, and recovery never creates a replacement Job, Turn, or prompt.

Completed results advance the Workflow through the existing task lifecycle exactly once, failed results enter declared recovery, and cancelled AgentJobs remain cancelled in the invocation projection while crossing the existing Workflow failure boundary; a repeated finalizer payload is Accepted/Stale without repeating variable mutation, artifact binding, or task application, while conflicting payloads stop as definitive Conflict.
Session runtime, transcript, activity, and terminal-close events remain audit facts and cannot independently complete, fail, cancel, or advance the Workflow.

Focused Server grain and integration tests cover every lifecycle state, every typed report disposition and Runner settlement decision, invalid-report terminal failure, terminal-delivery retry, duplicate/stale/conflicting result, bind commit followed by finalizer-receipt crash recovery, runner loss, unknown recovery, cancellation, permit release, and Workflow retry/recovery path.
tasks.output: Durable AgentJob-to-Workflow terminal arbitration with immutable status/result semantics and passing recovery tests.
tasks.notes: Use one AgentJob recovery reminder for PendingWorkflowTerminalDelivery and the explicit Accepted/Stale/Retry/Conflict acknowledgement contract; keep the typed finalization request immutable from the AgentJob report through delivery, recover bind results from the invocation-keyed bind receipt, and do not retain a separate ReceiveAgentJobResultAsync path or synthesize ordinary Runner task reports from transcript events.

tasks.title: Expose cross-owner Workflow Agent invocation projections
tasks.description: Implement the internal WorkflowAgentInvocationRead assembler and expose it through the existing Workflow task/run read surface or the selected dedicated route. Add Job and Session cross-links back to WorkflowRun and TaskRun, join canonical AgentJob facts with immutable Workflow lineage and Session initial-launch identities, and expose delivery application state without leaking Runner, Runtime Binding, workspace paths, prompts, transcript, or provider payloads.
acceptanceCriteria: The invocation read contains WorkflowRunId, TaskRunId, attempt, Job/Session/Input/Turn ids, Agent identity, session name, mapped status, reason, terminal result, workflowApplication, and observedAt.

A Workflow caller can locate the canonical AgentJob and AgentSession from the invocation, and AgentJob/AgentSession reads can locate the originating WorkflowRun and TaskRun without transcript parsing.

The projection joins status from AgentJob rather than persisting a second execution state machine; terminal AgentJob results are visible while workflowApplication=pending until Workflow acknowledgement arrives.
Nonterminal reads return result=null, terminal results remain stable across replay and Agent edits, and recovering work is represented without synthesizing success or failure.
Public read surfaces do not expose internal Runner identity, Runtime Binding, raw workspace paths, prompt content, transcript parts, or provider payloads.
Focused Server projection and API tests cover queued/executing/recovering/terminal states, cross-links, pending/applied/stale application acknowledgements, and absent terminal results.
tasks.output: Bidirectional Workflow/Agent invocation read projections and passing API/assembler tests.
tasks.notes: Resolve the open API-shape question during implementation by choosing either an embedded task DTO field or a dedicated route, then keep the read model internal and stable.

tasks.title: Complete legacy cutover, documentation, and end-to-end regression coverage
tasks.description: Apply the migration and cleanup plan after the new path is proven: preserve already-persisted concrete Inline Agent dispatch snapshots, route new mohist/agent attempts only through agent-handoff, and remove the old translator fallback and Workflow AgentSession reporter path once legacy work drains. Update the Agent execution/API, Action, and Session documentation and add end-to-end regression coverage for direct launches, inline Actions, checks, legacy draining, rollback behavior, and the complete Workflow-to-Agent lifecycle.
acceptanceCriteria: Existing persisted mohist/agent dispatch snapshots that already contain mohist/opencode or mohist/pi finish through the legacy path, while new TaskRun attempts create only agent-handoff work.

After the drain condition, the old WorkflowItemTranslator Agent fallback and Workflow AgentSession reporter advancement path are removed or unreachable for new invocations, with no second Agent scheduler or Runner-process protocol introduced.
Inline mohist/opencode and mohist/pi tasks, checks, unrelated Workflow Actions, direct Agent launches, Slack/Connection behavior, and external Agent API allowlists retain their existing semantics.

design/agent-execution.md, design/agent-api.md, docs/actions/agent.md, and docs/agent-sessions.md document the new ownership, identifiers, lifecycle/result contract, recovery rules, and breaking consumer change.

End-to-end tests cover valid and invalid Workflow inputs, Agent selection, queued/executing/terminal/recovering flow, stable lineage/result reads, Workflow expect/artifacts/setVars/recovery, stale delivery, and legacy cutover/rollback behavior.
The repository verification gate passes, or any environment limitation is recorded with the failing command and root cause.
tasks.output: Completed Workflow Agent cutover, updated documentation, end-to-end regression coverage, and a verified migration state.
tasks.notes: Do not backfill completed TaskRuns. Rollback stops new handoffs, lets accepted AgentJobs finish through the canonical ledger, and retains the terminal bridge until pending Workflow invocations drain.
